corrected_content.problem:
Evaluate the line integral $$
\displaystyle \int_(C)4yz\cos xds,
$$ where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $\mathbf{r}(t)=t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\operatorname{sin}t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}\hspace{0.167em}$ for $0 < t < \frac{π}{2}$.
corrected_content.worked_solution: Here $x=t$, $y=\sin t$, and $z=1$. The speed is $\sqrt{1+\cos^2t}$. Thus $$\int_C4yz\cos x\,ds=\int_0^{\pi/2}4\sin t\cos t\sqrt{1+\cos^2t}\,dt.$$ Set $u=1+\cos^2t$, so $du=-2\sin t\cos t\,dt$. The integral becomes $$2\int_1^2u^{1/2}\,du=\frac43(2\sqrt2-1).$$ The omitted endpoints have finite limits and do not change this value.
